references.text: Ezekiel prophesies that God will give the people a new heart and a new spirit, and remove the heart of stone - this expands on the promise of circumcision of the heart in Deuteronomy
Jeremiah speaks of the new covenant where God will put his law within them and write it on their hearts, as a fulfillment of the circumcision of the heart
Jeremiah urges Israel to circumcise themselves for the Lord, using the same terminology as in Deuteronomy 30:6
Moses urges Israel to circumcise the foreskin of their hearts and no longer be stubborn - a parallel exhortation to the promise in chapter 30
Paul writes about true circumcision that is of the heart, by the Spirit, not by the letter - a New Testament interpretation of the circumcision of the heart
Paul speaks of the circumcision in Christ, not made with hands, but by putting off the body of the sinful flesh - the fulfillment of the circumcision of the heart
The great commandment to love the Lord your God with all your heart and all your soul, which the circumcision of the heart in 30:6 is meant to make possible
Stephen accuses the Jews of being uncircumcised in heart and ears, showing the need for the circumcision that God promises in Deuteronomy
